name: Buckingham Webbing Friction Saver
title: Buckingham Webbing Friction Saver for Tree Climbing
meta: The Buckingham webbing friction saver uses tough webbing and two rings to protect the bark and your climbing line at the tie-in. Simple and proven.
tagline: Classic two-ring webbing cambium saver for climbers who want simple and reliable.
summary: The Buckingham webbing friction saver is a length of heavy webbing with a large ring on one end and a small ring on the other, set over a union so your rope runs through the rings instead of over the bark. It cuts wear on the tree and on your line, and it makes the climbing system run smoother on every advance.
highlights: Webbing strap with a large ring and a small ring
Keeps the climbing line off the bark at the tie-in point
Reduces rope wear and heat at the union
Retrievable from the ground with the right setup
Light and packs flat in a gear bag

body.h: How it works on the job
p: Install the saver over a sound union with the throw line, pull it up, and run your climbing line through both rings. The small ring follows the large ring when you retrieve it, so the saver comes down without leaving a tangle in the crown. Size the webbing so the rings sit close together without binding on a thick stem.

Compared with tying in directly over bark, a webbing saver keeps sap, grit and heat off your rope. That adds up over a season of moving-rope climbing, and it also keeps the cambium from getting burned by a line running back and forth all day.

Webbing has a flat profile that spreads the load over more bark than a rope saver, which is kind to thin-barked species. It also lies flat in a gear bag and does not hold a set the way some rope bodies do. Many climbers keep one in the kit even if their main saver is adjustable, simply because it is light and quick to install.

Check the webbing for cuts, glazing, chainsaw nicks and UV fade, and look at the stitching and rings for wear grooves before each climb. This is life-support gear. Use it only within the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133 practice, inspect it before every climb, and retire it when in doubt.
Webbing savers suit moderate stems and climbers who want the lightest option. If you work big leads often, compare adjustable models in our friction savers range.

faq.q: Can I use the Buckingham friction saver for SRS?
faq.a: It is built as a moving-rope tie-in point. For single-rope work, follow Buckingham's instructions and use a setup rated for that use.

faq.q: How do I get it out of the tree?
faq.a: With the right ring orientation and a retrieval setup, you pull the small-ring side and the saver comes down through the union. Practice on the ground first.

name: Clogger RopeGuard Chainsaw Protective Rope Sleeve
title: Clogger RopeGuard Chainsaw Protective Rope Sleeve
h1: Clogger RopeGuard Chainsaw Protective Rope Sleeve
meta: The Clogger RopeGuard is a cut-resistant sleeve that rides on your climbing line near the tie-in, adding protection where a saw is most likely to touch it.
tagline: Cut-resistant sleeve that adds a layer of protection to the line near your saw.
summary: The Clogger RopeGuard is a sleeve made from Clogger's cut-resistant fabric that slides over the climbing line close to your bridge, the part of the rope that sits nearest a running saw. It is a backup layer, not a license to cut near your line, but it buys margin on an awkward cut.
highlights: Cut-resistant fabric sleeve for the climbing line
Sits near the tie-in where saw contact risk is highest
Light enough to leave on the rope all day
Made by Clogger, known for chainsaw protective clothing
Adds margin on awkward one-handed positioning cuts

p: Most rope cuts happen close to the climber: reaching across the line for a limb, cutting near a lanyard, or a saw kicking back while the rope is pinned against the stem. The RopeGuard covers that short section, so a brush from the chain is more likely to grab fabric than to go straight through rope fibers.

Fit it so it can slide along the line but stays where you need it. Check that it does not interfere with your hitch, mechanical device or rope runner, and that it does not hide the rope from your inspection.

The sleeve is most useful for climbers who do a lot of work close to the tie-in: crown reductions, deadwooding and removals where you are cutting near your own line. On those jobs a small extra layer of protection costs little in weight and handling. It is a good addition to a kit for newer climbers who are still building saw-and-rope awareness.

No sleeve makes a rope chainsaw-proof. Keep your saw well clear of all life-support lines, use two points of attachment when cutting, and follow ANSI Z133 practice and your training. Inspect both the sleeve and the rope under it before every climb.
If the sleeve takes a cut, retire the sleeve and inspect the rope closely. Browse the rest of our friction savers and rope protection for other ways to protect the line.

faq.q: Does the RopeGuard make my rope cut-proof?
faq.a: No. It adds a protective layer that can slow or stop light chain contact. Saw discipline and two points of attachment are still the primary protection.

faq.q: Will it work with my climbing device?
faq.a: It sits on the rope below the device, but check fit with your hitch or mechanical device before climbing on it.

name: DMM Retrieval Cone
title: DMM Retrieval Cone for Friction Saver Retrieval
meta: The DMM retrieval cone helps friction savers and anchors slide out of the tree by guiding hardware through the union. A small part that saves stuck-gear grief.
tagline: A small cone that helps friction savers and anchors slide out of the tree cleanly.
summary: The DMM retrieval cone is a small tapered piece that sits on the line ahead of your hardware so it can slide through a narrow union instead of catching on bark or forks. It is a cheap add-on that makes ring savers and retrievable anchors come down more reliably.
highlights: Tapered shape guides hardware through tight unions
Cuts down on stuck friction savers and anchors
Light and simple, no moving parts
Lives on the line, so it is always there at retrieval
Made by DMM

p: Rings and connectors have flat faces that like to snag on bark ridges and tight crotches as they are pulled back over a union. A cone presents a smooth taper instead, so the hardware rolls up and over instead of hooking. The difference shows most in rough-barked species and in narrow V-shaped unions.

Set the cone so the taper leads the hardware in the direction it will travel on retrieval. Practice the retrieval on a low limb before you rely on it in a tall tree, and keep a throw line handy as a backup plan.

Climbers who use retrievable anchors for single-rope work tend to get the most from a cone, because a stuck anchor means a second climb or a long fight with the throw line. It is also handy for crews that climb conifers with rough bark and lots of small branch stubs around the union.

The cone is not part of the load path, but it shares space with life-support gear, so look it over during your daily inspection. Replace it if it cracks or the bore wears enough to slide out of position.
Pair it with a ring-and-ring saver or retrievable anchor from our friction savers section.

faq.q: Is the retrieval cone load-bearing?
faq.a: No. It is a retrieval aid. Your climbing system's load-rated parts carry the load.

faq.q: Will it fit my friction saver?
faq.a: It suits common ring-and-ring and retrievable setups, but check that it fits your rope diameter and hardware before use.

name: Fitch Saver Mid-Line Attachable Redirect
title: Fitch Saver Mid-Line Attachable Redirect for Climbers
meta: The Fitch Saver is a mid-line attachable redirect that clips onto your rope without an end, so you can add a redirect after you are already working in the tree.
tagline: Add a redirect mid-climb without untying or reaching for a rope end.
summary: The Fitch Saver is a mid-line attachable redirect, meaning you can put it on your climbing line anywhere along its length without feeding a rope end through it. That makes it handy for setting a redirect or protecting a union while you are already working in the crown.
highlights: Attaches mid-line, no rope end needed
Sets a redirect to improve your working angle
Keeps the line off the bark at the redirect
Useful for limb walks and wide crowns
Install and remove from your work position

p: A redirect changes the angle of your climbing line so you can reach the end of a long limb or work the far side of a crown without swinging. Normally that means a sling and carabiner, or feeding a rope end through hardware. A mid-line attachable unit skips that step, so you can set it from where you are and keep working.

Choose a sound limb that can take the force of a redirect, which can be higher than your body weight on a steep angle. Keep the redirect close enough to the main anchor that a slip does not produce a big swing.

Mid-line attachment also helps when your rope is already tied off at the base or rigged through other hardware. Instead of untying and re-threading, you add the redirect where you are, use it, and take it off on the way back. That saves time on big spreading crowns where you might set two or three redirects in one climb.

Read the manufacturer's instructions for rope diameter, loading direction and the systems it is rated for. This is life-support gear. Use it only within the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133 practice, inspect it before every climb, and retire it when in doubt. Practice clipping and unclipping on the ground before you use it aloft.
For other ways to protect the tie-in point, see our friction savers.

faq.q: Do I need the rope end to install the Fitch Saver?
faq.a: No. It is designed to attach mid-line, which is the main reason climbers choose it.

faq.q: Can it be used as a main anchor?
faq.a: Follow the maker's instructions on that. Most climbers use it as a redirect; use a rated anchor for your main tie-in.

name: KM Tree Adjustable Friction Saver
title: KM Tree Adjustable Friction Saver for Arborists
meta: An adjustable friction saver sets to the stem size so the rings sit right on big leads and small unions. The KM Tree version is built for moving-rope climbing.
tagline: Adjustable-length ring saver that fits a wide range of stem sizes.
summary: The KM Tree adjustable friction saver is a ring-and-ring saver with a length you can change, so one saver fits a skinny union and a thick lead. An adjustable friction saver keeps the rings in the right spot instead of riding loose on a small stem or barely reaching around a big one.
highlights: Adjustable length fits a wide range of stem sizes
Ring-and-ring design protects the bark and rope
Retrievable from the ground
One saver covers jobs a fixed saver cannot
Built for moving-rope tie-ins

p: A fixed-length saver works well on the stem size it was chosen for. Go smaller and the rings hang far apart, adding drag; go bigger and they may not reach around at all. An adjustable saver lets you snug the rings up on every tie-in, which keeps the rope running smoothly and limits wear on the bark.
Set the length on the ground if you can judge the stem from below, or adjust it at the anchor once you get there. Make sure the adjuster is set and dressed before you weight the system.

An adjustable saver also helps on trees where you plan to move your tie-in during the climb. Instead of carrying two fixed savers in different lengths, one adjustable unit covers the range. Expect it to weigh a little more and take a moment longer to set than a fixed webbing saver.

Check the rope or webbing body, the adjuster and both rings before every climb. Look for glazing, cuts, flat spots and grooves worn into the rings. This is life-support gear. Use it only within the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133 practice, inspect it before every climb, and retire it when in doubt.
Compare it with fixed and webbing models in our friction savers range.

faq.q: Can I retrieve an adjustable friction saver from the ground?
faq.a: Yes, with the correct ring setup. Practice retrieval on a low limb first.

faq.q: Is it for SRS?
faq.a: It is set up for moving rope. Use only systems the maker rates for single-rope work.

name: Teufelberger Equaliza
title: Teufelberger Equaliza Adjustable Anchor Sling
meta: The Teufelberger Equaliza is an adjustable anchor sling for building a tie-in across two stems or limbs, sharing the load instead of trusting a single union.
tagline: Adjustable anchor that shares your tie-in across two attachment points.
summary: The Teufelberger Equaliza is an adjustable anchor sling for building a tie-in point across two stems, limbs or unions so the load is shared rather than resting on one. It suits trees where no single crotch inspires confidence, or where you want a centered anchor between two leads.
highlights: Builds a shared anchor across two attachment points
Adjustable to fit different spacing and stem sizes
Helps center the tie-in between two leads
Made by Teufelberger, the maker of well-known arborist ropes
Packs small in a gear bag

p: Codominant stems, wide-spreading oaks and trees with smaller leads all make a single crotch a poor anchor. Spreading the load across two points lowers the force on each and lets you place your tie-in where it gives the best working angle. The Equaliza makes that quicker to rig than tying slings and knots aloft.

Keep the angle between the two legs narrow. As the angle opens, the force on each leg rises, which defeats the point of sharing the load. Size the setup so the master point sits where you want your rope to run.

Two-point anchors are also useful for redirecting the load toward the center of the tree on removals and heavy reductions, where you want the tie-in as close to the trunk as you can get it. Assess both attachment points as carefully as you would a single anchor; sharing the load does not make a weak limb safe.

Follow Teufelberger's instructions for how to set and adjust it, which systems it is rated for and how to connect your rope. This is life-support gear. Use it only within the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133 practice, inspect it before every climb, and retire it when in doubt.
See our full range of friction savers and anchors for single-point options.

faq.q: Does the Equaliza replace a friction saver?
faq.a: It does a different job: it builds an anchor across two points. Use it where a single union is not ideal.

faq.q: Can it be retrieved from the ground?
faq.a: Check Teufelberger's instructions. Many two-point anchors need to be removed from aloft.

name: Teufelberger fimbCLIMB
title: Teufelberger fimbCLIMB Friction Saver and Anchor
meta: The Teufelberger fimbCLIMB is an anchor and friction saver system that protects the tie-in point and keeps your climbing line running clean through the crown.
tagline: Teufelberger anchor system for protecting the tie-in point and your climbing line.
summary: The Teufelberger fimbCLIMB is an anchor system that protects the tree and your climbing line at the tie-in point, so rope runs through hardware instead of over bark. It comes from Teufelberger, whose climbing lines are used by tree crews around the world.
highlights: Protects the bark and line at the tie-in
Teufelberger construction and instructions
Smoother rope travel than tying over bark
Suited to everyday climbing work
Compact enough to carry on every job

p: Every time a moving rope runs over bark, it picks up grit, builds heat and polishes the cambium. Putting hardware at the tie-in avoids that, keeps your rope cleaner and makes ascents and repositioning smoother. On trees you climb repeatedly, it also leaves less damage for the client to see.
Set the fimbCLIMB over a sound union, run your line as shown in Teufelberger's instructions and check that every connector is closed and loaded along its long axis before you leave the ground.

On trees you return to every year, protecting the anchor also leaves less visible wear on the bark, which matters to homeowners and to the long-term health of the tree. A good anchor setup is one of the cheapest ways to extend the life of an expensive climbing line.

Read Teufelberger's user information for the rope diameters and climbing systems it is rated for. This is life-support gear. Use it only within the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133 practice, inspect it before every climb, and retire it when in doubt.

Teufelberger also publishes inspection guidance for its life-support products. Keep a copy with your gear records, and log the date the fimbCLIMB goes into service so retirement decisions are based on facts rather than guesswork.
Compare it with other options in our friction savers range to match your style of climbing.

faq.q: Which climbing systems does the fimbCLIMB work with?
faq.a: Use it only with the systems and rope sizes listed in Teufelberger's instructions.

faq.q: How often should I inspect it?
faq.a: Before every climb, and in a documented inspection at the interval your employer or the maker sets.

name: Teufelberger Pulleysaver Replacement Lanyard
title: Teufelberger Pulleysaver Replacement Lanyard
meta: Replace worn rope on your Teufelberger Pulleysaver with a genuine replacement lanyard and keep the pulley and hardware in service for more seasons of climbing.
tagline: Genuine replacement rope for the Teufelberger Pulleysaver adjustable saver.
summary: The Teufelberger Pulleysaver replacement lanyard is the rope section that connects the pulley and ring on a Pulleysaver. The hardware usually outlasts the rope, so a new lanyard puts the whole unit back to work without buying a complete saver.
highlights: Genuine replacement part for the Pulleysaver
Keeps good hardware in service
Cheaper than a complete new saver
Restores smooth adjustment and a clean rope body
Teufelberger construction

p: The rope on a friction saver takes abuse: bark abrasion, sap, sun and grit worked in by the climbing line. Replace the lanyard when the cover is glazed, fuzzed deep into the strands, stiff, cut or flattened, or when you cannot confidently say it is sound. A tired lanyard is the usual reason a Pulleysaver gets retired.
Inspect the pulley sheave, side plates and ring before you fit the new lanyard. If the hardware is grooved, cracked or the sheave does not spin freely, replace that too.

Keeping a spare lanyard on the truck also means a damaged saver does not end the climb. If the rope takes a nick from a saw or catches a sharp edge, you can swap it on the ground and keep working instead of switching to a different system mid-job.

Assemble the lanyard and hardware exactly as Teufelberger's instructions show, and check the finished saver on the ground before you climb on it. This is life-support gear. Use it only within the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133 practice, inspect it before every climb, and retire it when in doubt.
Log the date you fit the new lanyard. A simple record of when each part went into service makes it much easier to decide when the next replacement is due.
Find complete savers and other options in our friction savers section.

faq.q: Will this lanyard fit other pulley savers?
faq.a: It is made for the Teufelberger Pulleysaver. Do not adapt it to other brands.

faq.q: Do I need to replace the pulley too?
faq.a: Only if inspection shows wear, cracks or a sheave that does not turn freely.

name: Arbortec Python 50L Backpack Gear Bag
title: Arbortec Python 50L Backpack Gear Bag for Arborists
meta: The Arbortec Python 50L backpack carries a saddle, hardware and rope to the job on your back, leaving your hands free for saws and throw line kits on the walk.
tagline: A 50L backpack that hauls a full climbing kit into the backyard on your shoulders.
summary: The Arbortec Python 50L backpack is a gear bag with shoulder straps, sized to carry a saddle, connectors, hitch cords and spare rope from the truck to the tree. On jobs with a long walk through gates and gardens, carrying the kit on your back beats juggling a duffel and a saw.
highlights: 50 liter capacity for a full climbing kit
Backpack straps for long walks to the tree
Keeps gear together and out of the dirt
Rugged construction for truck and job life
Made by Arbortec, a tree-care clothing and kit brand

body.h: Carrying a kit to the tree
p: Residential jobs rarely let you park next to the tree. A backpack keeps the weight on your hips and shoulders over a long carry, and keeps both hands free for a saw, a throw line kit or a rope bag. Fifty liters takes a saddle with hardware attached plus a bundle of hitch cords and slings.
Pack the heavy items close to your back and keep connectors and cords bagged so nothing snags in transit. At the tree, open the bag on a tarp so small parts stay out of the leaf litter.

A backpack also suits climbers who move between crews or travel to storm work, where gear gets packed and unpacked every day. Keeping one kit in one bag makes it easy to see when something is missing before you leave the yard.

Life-support gear lasts longer when it rides in a bag instead of loose in a truck bed with fuel cans and chain oil. Dry the bag and its contents after a wet day, and keep chemicals away from your saddle and ropes.

Buy a bag sized for what you actually carry. Too small and gear gets crammed in and stays damp; too big and things slide around and get lost at the bottom. If you run separate climbing and rigging kits, a bag for each keeps the two from mixing.
Browse more gear bags if you need a different size or style.

faq.q: Will a saddle fit in the Arbortec Python 50L?
faq.a: Yes, it is sized for a saddle with some hardware and cords, though a very large kit may need a second bag.

faq.q: Can I carry rope in it too?
faq.a: A short rope fits alongside smaller gear. A full climbing line usually rides better in a dedicated rope bag.

name: Petzl Duffel 65L Transport Bag
title: Petzl Duffel 65L Transport Bag for Climbing Gear
meta: The Petzl Duffel 65 is a tough 65 liter transport bag for climbing kits, with a wide opening for fast packing and straps to carry it like a backpack.
tagline: A rugged 65L duffel that carries a full climbing kit and rope to the job.
summary: The Petzl Duffel 65 is a 65 liter transport bag built from heavy coated fabric, with a wide opening and carry straps that let you haul it by hand or on your back. It swallows a saddle, a climbing line and a set of hardware, which makes it a solid one-bag kit for a climber.
highlights: 65 liter capacity for saddle, rope and hardware
Heavy coated fabric stands up to truck beds
Wide opening for quick packing and unpacking
Carry by hand or with backpack straps
Made by Petzl

p: Plenty of climbers like to keep everything for the day in a single bag: saddle, climbing line, friction saver, hitch cords and spare connectors. A 65 liter duffel is big enough for that without turning into a sack you cannot lift. The wide opening means you can see what is inside without dumping it on the ground.
Pack the rope at the bottom and the saddle on top so you can pull the saddle out first at the tree. Keep sharp tools, files and handsaws in a separate case so they cannot nick your rope in transit.

A duffel this size also makes a good home for a full storm or travel kit, where you need to carry spare cords, a second saddle bridge or a backup friction saver. The tough fabric shrugs off gravel, wet grass and the bed of a truck far better than a light backpack.
The coated fabric wipes clean of sap and mud. Let the bag and your gear dry fully before closing it up after a wet job, and store it out of direct sun.

Buy a bag sized for what you actually carry. Too small and gear gets crammed in and stays damp; too big and things slide around and get lost at the bottom. If you run separate climbing and rigging kits, a bag for each keeps the two from mixing.
See our other gear bags for smaller backpacks and rope bags.

faq.q: Is the Petzl Duffel 65 big enough for a rope and saddle?
faq.a: Yes, it is sized to carry a typical climbing line with a saddle and hardware.

faq.q: Can it be carried as a backpack?
faq.a: Yes, it has straps for carrying on your back as well as handles.

name: Weaver Cavern Gear Bag
title: Weaver Cavern Gear Bag for Climbing Kits
meta: The Weaver Cavern gear bag is a roomy bag for hauling a saddle, rope and hardware between truck and tree. Simple, tough and sized for a full climbing kit.
tagline: A roomy, tough bag for keeping a climbing kit together and off the truck floor.
summary: The Weaver Cavern gear bag is a large, open-top style bag made to hold a climber's saddle, hardware and rope in one place. Weaver has been making saddles and climbing gear for tree crews for a long time, and this bag is built for the same daily truck-and-job routine.
highlights: Roomy body for saddle, rope and hardware
Tough fabric for daily truck use
Keeps gear together and out of the dirt
Easy to see and reach what is inside
Made by Weaver

p: Climbing gear left loose in a truck gets stepped on, soaked in bar oil and buried under brush. A gear bag keeps your saddle, rope and connectors together and protected, so you can grab one bag and go. It also makes daily inspection easier when everything comes out of the same place.
Keep chemicals, fuel and sharp tools out of the bag. A file or handsaw rattling around next to your climbing line is a good way to find a cut you did not expect.

The roomy opening makes daily inspection easier, too. Pull everything out at the end of the day, check it over and pack it back in a set order, so you know at a glance when a carabiner or hitch cord is missing.
Put the rope in first and the saddle on top, with carabiners and devices clipped to a gear loop so they do not end up loose at the bottom. Let everything dry before you close the bag after a wet day.

Buy a bag sized for what you actually carry. Too small and gear gets crammed in and stays damp; too big and things slide around and get lost at the bottom. If you run separate climbing and rigging kits, a bag for each keeps the two from mixing.
Shop the rest of our gear bags for backpacks and duffels.

faq.q: What fits in the Weaver Cavern gear bag?
faq.a: It is sized for a saddle, hardware and a climbing line. Very long ropes may need their own bag.

faq.q: How should I clean it?
faq.a: Brush off debris and wipe it with mild soap and water, then let it air dry out of the sun.

name: Edelrid Caddy II Rope Bag
title: Edelrid Caddy II Rope Bag for Climbing Lines
meta: The Edelrid Caddy II rope bag keeps your climbing line clean, flaked and ready to deploy, with a sturdy body that stands open at the base of the tree.
tagline: A rope bag that keeps your climbing line clean, flaked and ready to run.
summary: The Edelrid Caddy II is a rope bag that holds a climbing line flaked and ready to feed out at the base of the tree. Keeping rope in a bag instead of piled in the dirt cuts down on grit working into the fibers, and it means the line pays out without knots when you need it.
highlights: Keeps rope clean and flaked for fast deployment
Stands open at the base of the tree
Cuts down on grit and debris in the rope
Easy to carry between truck and tree
Made by Edelrid

p: Dirt is a slow killer for climbing rope. Grit works into the braid and grinds fibers from the inside every time the rope bends. A rope bag keeps the line off the ground at the tree and in the truck, and it keeps the rope flaked so it feeds out cleanly instead of coming up as a bird's nest.
Flake the rope into the bag from the end that will be tied off last, so the working end comes out on top. Clip the tail to the bag's tie-in point if it has one so you always know where the end is.

A rope bag also protects the line from the things that sit in a work truck: fuel, bar oil, battery acid and sharp tools. Many climbers keep one bag per rope so it is always clear which line is which, and how much of the season it has seen.
Empty the bag regularly and shake out debris. If your rope gets wet, let it dry loosely out of the sun before bagging it for storage.

When you flake rope into the bag, run your hands along it. Bagging is a natural time to feel for flat spots, stiff sections, cuts and glazing, and to catch damage before the next climb rather than at the top of the tree.
See more rope bags for different sizes and carry styles.

faq.q: How much rope fits in the Edelrid Caddy II?
faq.a: It is made for a climbing line. Capacity depends on rope diameter and length, so check before buying for long ropes.

faq.q: Should I store my rope in the bag?
faq.a: Yes, once it is dry. Keep the bag out of direct sun and away from chemicals.

name: Husqvarna Backpack Rope Bag 30L
title: Husqvarna Backpack Rope Bag 30L for Climbers
meta: The Husqvarna backpack rope bag holds 30L and carries your climbing line to the tree, keeping it clean, flaked and ready to feed out without tangles.
tagline: A 30L backpack rope bag that keeps your line clean and your hands free.
summary: The Husqvarna backpack rope bag is a 30 liter bag that holds a climbing line flaked and ready to deploy. Carry it on your shoulders to the tree, set it down at the base and the rope feeds out clean, without picking up dirt and sawdust from the ground.
highlights: 30 liter capacity for a climbing line
Backpack straps for carrying to the tree
Keeps rope clean and flaked
Opens wide for flaking and feeding
Made by Husqvarna

p: Rope rides best in its own bag. The backpack style lets you carry a climbing line on your shoulders while your hands handle a saw and throw line kit. At the tree, open it up and the rope pays out from the top as you install your line, then flake it back in when you come down.
Thirty liters suits a typical climbing line. If you carry a long line or a thick rigging rope, check the length and diameter against the bag before you count on it.
A dedicated rope bag also helps you keep track of rope history. One rope, one bag, and a tag with the date it went into service makes logging inspections much simpler for a climber or a crew lead.
Grit inside the braid wears rope from the inside, and a bag is the easiest way to keep it out. Shake out the bag often and dry wet rope before storing it.

When you flake rope into the bag, run your hands along it. Bagging is a natural time to feel for flat spots, stiff sections, cuts and glazing, and to catch damage before the next climb rather than at the top of the tree.
Shop our other rope bags for larger capacities.

faq.q: Will the Husqvarna rope bag hold a full climbing line?
faq.a: It is sized for a typical climbing line. Very long or thick ropes may need a larger bag.

faq.q: Can I store gear in it as well?
faq.a: A few small items fit, but keep sharp tools away from the rope.

name: Weaver XL Rope Bag
title: Weaver XL Rope Bag for Climbing and Rigging Rope
meta: The Weaver XL rope bag gives long climbing lines and rigging rope a clean place to live, flaked and ready to feed out at the tree. Simple, sturdy and roomy.
tagline: Extra-large rope bag for long climbing lines and rigging rope.
summary: The Weaver XL rope bag is a large bag for long climbing lines and rigging rope that will not fit in a standard bag. It keeps the rope clean and flaked so it runs out without tangles, whether you are setting a climbing line or feeding a lowering line to the ground crew.
highlights: Extra-large size for long or thick ropes
Keeps rope clean and tangle-free
Works for climbing and rigging lines
Sturdy build for daily truck use
Made by Weaver

p: Tall trees and big removals call for long ropes, and long ropes are the ones that tangle worst when they are piled loose. An XL bag gives a full-length climbing line or a rigging rope room to sit flaked, so the ground crew can feed it without stopping to pick knots.

Label bags by rope so nobody grabs a rigging line when they meant to grab a climbing line. Keep the two separate: rigging rope sees shock loads and abrasion that you do not want in a life-support line.

name: 6mm Ocean Polyester Thimble Loop
title: 6mm Ocean Polyester Thimble Loop Prusik Cord
meta: The 6mm Ocean Polyester thimble loop is a small polyester cord loop with a thimble eye, handy for gear attachments and accessory jobs around your kit.
tagline: Small polyester loop with a thimble eye for accessory attachments.
summary: The 6mm Ocean Polyester thimble loop is a short loop of 6 mm polyester cord with a thimble protecting the eye. It is an accessory piece for attaching small gear and making tidy connections around your saddle and kit, where a thimble keeps a connector from wearing the cord.
highlights: 6 mm polyester cord
Thimble protects the eye from connector wear
Handy for accessory attachments
Compact and light
Easy to add to an existing kit

p: Small loops solve lots of small problems: hanging a handsaw, clipping a bag to a saddle, or making a neat connection for accessory gear. A thimble in the eye keeps a carabiner from pinching and wearing the cord, so the loop lasts longer and the connector sits where you want it.
Six millimeter cord is accessory size. Use it for gear and accessory jobs, not as a climbing hitch or a life-support connection unless the maker's rating and instructions specifically allow it.

Polyester cord holds its shape and resists stretch and sun better than many nylon cords, which suits small loops that live on a saddle all season. Keep a couple in the kit so one is always on hand for a quick fix.

Check the cord for cuts and fuzzing and make sure the thimble is seated and not cracked or deformed. Replace the loop if either is damaged. Anything clipped into your life-support system still has to meet ANSI Z133 practice and the maker's instructions.
Label or color-code your accessory loops so they never get mistaken for rated hitch cords or slings when someone grabs gear in a hurry.

faq.q: Can I use a 6mm thimble loop as a climbing hitch?
faq.a: No. Six millimeter cord is accessory size. Use a hitch cord rated for climbing for your friction hitch.

faq.q: What does the thimble do?
faq.a: It protects the eye from wear and pinching where a connector clips in.
